_spec.purpose: A standalone web edition of the archived visual story.
_spec.law: Facts resolve to the original verified claim record. A layout rebuild does not reverify reporting.

dek.text: A proposed Texas grid service would buy demand reductions from large electricity users. Its definition turns on a site's power demand, not whether it is called a data center.

introduction.text: The Public Utility Commission's proposed [Large Load Demand Management Service](c1) addresses a problem larger than a single industry. It would require ERCOT to procure demand reductions from qualifying electricity users when an emergency is anticipated.

The published proposal does not use the words data center. It defines a large load customer by total non-coincident peak demand at a single site. That definition determines the proposed service's reach.

paragraphs.text: ERCOT would competitively procure demand reductions under an annual budget limit. The proposal also calls for a protocol allowing transmission-voltage customers to be curtailed during firm load shedding. A proposed service is not yet an adopted operating rule.
The distinction matters for reading the docket. The proposal is about demand management. The presence of data center companies among the filers does not rewrite the published customer definition.

sections.heading: A filing list is not a position summary

paragraphs.text: The [Interchange index](c7) identifies parties, filing dates and short descriptions. It includes companies, individuals and a university-affiliated filer. Those entries establish that documents were submitted, not everything their authors argued.

The proposal directs electronic comments through the commission's interchange and requires the project number. Its notice sets the comment deadline at {{date:c2}}. That was the participation window as published for this edition.
The final rule would establish which proposed requirements survive the comment process. Until adoption is verified, the definition, budget and curtailment provisions should be read as proposed terms.
